What is Python Programming? (Python क्या है?) Guido van Rossum created the high-level, interpreted, open-source Python programming language in 1991. It was created with a single, straightforward objective: to make programming simple and readable for everyone. Unlike many languages that require complex syntax, Python reads almost like English. For example: print(“Hello, World!”) This one line of code displays “Hello, World!” on the screen — no semicolons, no confusing symbols, just pure simplicity. Master coding skills through expert-led Python training in Pune. Important Python Features Python is a popular programming language because of its ease of use and readability. Here are a few of its salient characteristics: 1. Easy to Learn and Use: Beginners can easily learn Python because to its simple syntax. 2. Versatile : It may be applied to a wide range of tasks, such as scientific computing, web development, data analysis, artificial intelligence, and more. 3. Large Standard Library : Python has an extensive standard library that makes programming activities easier and supports a wide range of applications. 4. Cross-Platform: Python can run code on multiple platforms without requiring any changes because it is compatible with a wide range of operating systems. 5. Dynamic Typing: Python variables are flexible and simpler to use because they don’t need an explicit declaration of their type. 6. Community Support: Python boasts a sizable and vibrant community that adds to a vast library and framework collection. 7. Object-Oriented: Python allows for object-oriented programming, which facilitates effective code organisation and structuring. Python is a popular choice among developers and organisations worldwide because of these qualities. • Simple to Learn: No prior programming experience is required. • Adaptable: Used in automation, web development, artificial intelligence, and data science. • Cross-Platform: Compatible with Linux, Mac, and Windows. • A wide range of libraries, including TensorFlow, NumPy, Pandas, and Django. Python’s beauty lies in how quickly you can go from learning basics to creating something meaningful — whether it’s a website, an app, or a machine learning model. Why Python is So Popular in 2025 Python’s popularity has exploded in recent years. According to TIOBE and Stack Overflow rankings, Python has consistently been among the top 3 most-used languages worldwide. Here’s why developers love Python: Beginner-Friendly: Python is intuitive, making it the ideal language for students and non-IT learners. High Demand: Top companies like Google, Netflix, Amazon, and Infosys rely on Python for automation, analytics, and AI. Strong Career Scope: With roles like Data Analyst, Python Developer, and Machine Learning Engineer, job opportunities are massive. Community Support: If you ever get stuck, you’ll find solutions easily through online forums and Python groups.Get guided mentorship and learn Python from experts 💬 In short, Python has become the “universal language” of coding — simple, powerful, and future-proof. Applications of Python in the Real World Python is not just a language; it is a tool powering many of the applications and technologies you use every day. Let us explore its practical uses: Domain Python Applications Web Development Websites using Django and Flask frameworks Data Science Data analysis, visualization, and prediction using Pandas & Matplotlib Machine Learning AI models built using TensorFlow and Scikit-learn Automation Writing scripts to automate repetitive tasks Cybersecurity Building penetration testing tools Finance Risk modeling, forecasting, and stock analysis Game Development Creating simple games using Pygame This versatility is what makes Python a must-learn skill for the future. Learn Python in Hindi – From Basics to Advanced If English feels challenging, don’t worry — you can easily learn Python in Hindi with our step-by-step video and training sessions. Step 1: Understand the Basics Start with concepts like: Variables Data types (strings, integers, lists, dictionaries) Loops (for, while) Conditional statements (if-else) These are the building blocks of every program. Step 2: Practice Simple Programs This teaches you how loops work. Step 3: Explore Python Libraries Once you’re comfortable, explore libraries like: NumPy – for numerical operations Pandas – for data analysis Matplotlib – for data visualization Flask/Django – for web development Step 4: Work on Projects Projects turn theory into skill. Here are some trending roles: 1. Python Developer: Builds web applications, backend systems, and APIs using frameworks like Django and Flask. 2. Data Analyst / Data Scientist: Analyzes business data using Python libraries like Pandas, NumPy, and Matplotlib. 3. Machine Learning Engineer: Develops AI models using Scikit-learn and TensorFlow. 4. Automation Engineer: Creates scripts to automate IT and business processes. 5. Web Developer: Designs responsive web apps with HTML, CSS, and Python-based backends. 6. Software Tester (Automation): Uses Python with Selenium for automated testing.According to Indeed, the average salary for Python developers in India ranges from ₹5 LPA to ₹15 LPA, depending on their experience and skills.
